question: A 36-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-week history of progressively worsening pain on the outer side of her left elbow. She does not recall any trauma to the area. The patient plays badminton recreationally. Examination shows tenderness over the lateral surface of the left distal humerus. The pain is reproduced by supinating the forearm against resistance. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's pain?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Repetitive supination against resistance" -> "Lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow)" -> "Pain on the outer side of the elbow" -> "Excessive stress to the bone" -> 80% CHAIN: "Repetitive wrist extension" -> "Lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow)" -> "Pain on the outer side of the elbow" -> "Excessive stress to the bone" -> 75% CHAIN: "Repetitive wrist flexion" -> "Medial epicondylitis (golfer's elbow)" -> "Pain on the inner side of the elbow" -> "Excessive stress to the bone" -> 80%
enhanced_information: The most likely underlying cause of this patient's pain is lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow) due to repetitive supination against resistance. This condition is characterized by pain on the outer side of the elbow and is not directly related to excessive stress to the bone, nerve compression at the elbow, bursal inflammation, repeated wrist extension, or repeated wrist flexion.
analysis: The patient's presentation of pain on the outer side of the left elbow, tenderness over the lateral surface of the left distal humerus, and pain reproduced by supinating the forearm against resistance are classic signs of lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow). This condition is commonly seen in individuals who engage in activities involving repetitive wrist extension and supination. The enhanced information provided aligns with the known facts about lateral epicondylitis, making it the most likely underlying cause of the patient's pain.
